abort_reason.summary: Architectural framing wrong: persona-roles (Employee, Manager) are SURFACES WITHIN SaaS products (HR, Payroll, Hiring), not standalone 'experience µservices'.
abort_reason.correct_architecture: SaaS product catalog (AWS-service-catalog model). HR is a full SaaS product; Employee/Manager are roles/surfaces within HR + Payroll + Hiring products. The persona-experience-µservice anti-pattern dissolves persona slices into the SaaS products that own the underlying entities and workflows.
abort_reason.anti_pattern_avoided: Creating a standalone µservice keyed on persona (Employee, Manager) rather than on bounded SaaS product. Repeating this would have inverted ADR-0132's no-suite policy intent (single-concern µservices) by introducing 'persona-suite' µservices through the back door.

lessons_emitted_for_coordinator_use: Persona-named µservices (Employee, Manager, Customer) are an anti-pattern when SaaS products already own the underlying entities and workflows. Persona slices are surfaces WITHIN products, not products themselves.

The Workflow Studio + Ontology adapter pattern (per memory #workflow_objectgraph_adapter_layer) is the correct integration substrate for cross-product manager surfaces (single approval inbox, calibration). Adapter, not new µservice.
Mobile-first PWA + native is a channel discipline (ADR-0185), not a µservice boundary. Apply per-product.
AI-as-assist tier discipline (T0/T1 only, EU AI Act limited-risk) survives the abort and applies to ANY SaaS product surfacing AI on employment-related decisions.
PRD discipline (persona-needs-first, competitor-parity-last, integrity-bar) is portable — the salvage payload can seed three SaaS product PRDs without reauthoring the persona walk-throughs.
